product_scope: YAZIO AI Food Recognition is a Pro feature that analyzes a meal photo, detects ingredients, estimates initial portions and nutrition, and lets the user edit ingredients, quantities, and meal name before saving. YAZIO explicitly calls the result a rough estimate.
supported_platforms: Android and iOS. The public Android artifact analyzed was package com.yazio.android, version 26.29.0.
pricing: The AI food-recognition feature is part of YAZIO Pro; consumer subscription price varies by market and offer. No public developer API price for YAZIO's internal service was found. Source: https://help.yazio.com/hc/en-us/articles/39137901903889-What-is-the-AI-Calorie-Tracking-Feature-and-how-does-it-work
popularity_signal: YAZIO markets a large food database and AI photo logging, but scanner-specific usage and accuracy metrics were not publicly disclosed in the sources checked.
recognition_behavior: Photo -> AI detects ingredients -> initial portion/nutrition estimate -> user adjusts ingredients and amount -> meal is saved or templated. The Android resource strings also state that photos are not stored or shared, that the AI was trained on millions of meals, and that users can have a daily AI-prompt limit.
identified_services: YAZIO's current privacy policy names OpenAI Ireland Ltd. as the technical service provider for YAZIO AI functions and says data may be transmitted to OpenAI servers. It does not explicitly document which exact photo-scanner request or model is used, so an OpenAI connection is high-confidence for YAZIO AI generally but not fully mapped to every scanner path. Sources: https://www.yazio.com/en/privacy and https://help.yazio.com/hc/en-us/articles/39137901903889-What-is-the-AI-Calorie-Tracking-Feature-and-how-does-it-work
model_or_provider_confidence: [uncertain] OpenAI Ireland is explicitly named for YAZIO AI functions; the exact OpenAI model, image endpoint, prompt, and whether a separate food model is used are not publicly specified.
local_inference_evidence: YAZIO's photo workflow and privacy policy provide a strong cloud-processing signal, while the public Android XAPK contains no obvious food VLM/model assets. The base APK includes ML Kit barcode assets/classes, which appear unrelated to food-photo understanding. Runtime downloads cannot be ruled out.
portion_and_nutrition_method: YAZIO documents initial estimates from detected ingredients and asks the user to enter the most accurate portion sizes/amounts. It does not claim measurement-grade calories or grams. Nutrition is presumably resolved through YAZIO's food database after the AI candidate step; the exact data pipeline is not public.

static_findings: The base APK has CAMERA and INTERNET permissions, AI food-tracking/photo-upload resources, CameraX image-analysis code, and bundled ML Kit barcode models/classes. No obvious food VLM/classifier model file was found in the XAPK inventory. The app is heavily obfuscated, so static endpoint/provider attribution is limited.
reverse_engineering_limits: No installation, execution, account login, traffic capture, or authentication bypass was attempted. Static assets cannot prove whether a cloud request happens for a particular feature flag or whether models are downloaded later.
candidate_models: For SuperNutrition, evaluate a local food classifier/segmenter first; use Gemma 3n E2B or SmolVLM as optional local semantic fallbacks, Apple Foundation Models on supported iOS, and Gemini Nano on supported Android. Use a nutrition database for final nutrients.
mobile_runtime_support: Core ML, LiteRT, ExecuTorch, and ONNX Runtime Mobile can host local vision models. ONNX Runtime supports Android and iOS packages and Core ML/XNNPACK or NNAPI/XNNPACK accelerators. Source: https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/tutorials/mobile/
device_requirements: A compact classifier is broadly deployable; a 2B-4B multimodal model should be limited to modern high-memory devices and measured for sustained battery/thermal behavior.
expected_food_inference_quality: YAZIO itself warns that outputs are rough. Common visible foods should be easier than recipe composition, hidden sauces/oils, mixed dishes, unfamiliar cuisine, and portion size.
unit_cost_estimate: [uncertain] YAZIO's negotiated OpenAI cost is not public. As a reference, current OpenAI image-capable API pricing is metered by image tokens plus output tokens; this is not a YAZIO-specific rate. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-mini
privacy_and_compliance: YAZIO's policy says OpenAI Ireland is the technical provider, data may reach US servers under EU transfer safeguards, and data sent through OpenAI's API is not used to train general OpenAI models. Product copy also says photos are not stored or shared. Treat these as vendor disclosures that must be contractually verified for SuperNutrition.
recommendation: YAZIO is a useful reference architecture: cloud AI candidate generation, explicit rough-estimate disclaimer, and user correction. Replicate the confirmation UX and make local/cloud routing explicit rather than copying the hidden provider boundary.
